prompt: A phone costs $\$600$ new. It loses $25\%$ of its value every year. What is it worth after $2$ years, in dollars?
hint: Losing $25\%$ means keeping $75\%$. Turn that into a decay factor.

hints.text: Losing $25\%$ means keeping $75\%$. Turn that into a decay factor.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: a $\$100$ item that loses $50\%$ a year is worth $\$50$ after one year and $\$25$ after two. Same move — multiply by the keep-factor once per year.
Year 2: $450 \times 0.75 = 337.5$, so the phone is worth $\$337.50$.

explanation: Losing $25\%$ means $75\%$ stays, so the decay factor is $0.75$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Subtract a quarter each year
steps: A quarter of $600$ is $150$, so year 1 ends at $600 - 150 = 450$.
A quarter of $450$ is $112.50$, so year 2 ends at $450 - 112.50 = 337.50$.
The drop gets smaller each year because it is a percent of a smaller number.

alternativeExplanations.title: One power instead of two steps
steps: Two years of the same factor is $0.75^2$.
